glossary.bands: Lexical frequency bands: how much of the text is covered by the most frequent words (1,000, 2,000...).
glossary.cohens_d: Cohen's d: effect size in standard deviations. About 0.2 = small; 0.5 = medium; 0.8 = large.
glossary.collocate: Collocate: a word that often appears near the searched word (the node).
glossary.dp_gries: Gries' DP: standard deviation of a word's positions in the corpus. High = spread out; low = concentrated.
glossary.kfa: KFA (Key Feature Analysis): compares groups feature by feature using effect size (Cohen's d).
glossary.keyness: Keyness: how characteristic a word is of one corpus compared with another (reference).
glossary.lemma: Lemma: the dictionary form of a word ("made" → "make"). In queries, lemma=make finds every form.
glossary.lexical_density: Lexical density: share of content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) in the text.
glossary.lexical_diversity: Lexical diversity: ratio of different words to total words (types/tokens). High = more varied vocabulary.
glossary.ll: Log-likelihood (LL): how much more often an item appears next to the node than expected by chance. Higher = stronger association.
glossary.log_odds: Log-odds: relative chances of a word occurring in one corpus rather than the other.
glossary.log_ratio: Log ratio: size of the frequency difference between two corpora.
glossary.mi: Mutual information (MI): strength of association between two words; favours rare pairs. Higher = more tightly bound.
glossary.ngram: N-gram: a run of N consecutive words. n=2 is a pair; n=3 a triple.
glossary.per_1000: Frequency per 1,000 words: normalises by size so you can compare texts and corpora of different sizes.
glossary.percent_diff: %DIFF: percentage difference between the normalised frequencies of two corpora.
glossary.phrase: Phrase (query in quotes): an exact sequence of words, e.g. "black cat".
glossary.pos: Part of speech (POS): for example NOUN, VERB, ADJ. In queries, pos=NOUN restricts to the class.
glossary.query: How to query: word (matches the form), word* (starts with), /regex/ (pattern), lemma= (lemma), pos=CLASS (part of speech), tag=TAG (fine tag) and "phrase" (exact sequence). Join terms with a space.
glossary.range: Range: in what share of texts (%) the word appears. High = present in almost all.
glossary.regex: Regular expression: a search pattern. /ca.t/ finds "cat", "cart"; /^the$/ only the exact word.
glossary.stopwords: Stopwords (function words): very frequent grammatical items (articles, prepositions), low information.
glossary.t_score: T-score: confidence in the association; favours frequent pairs. Higher = safer.
glossary.tag: Fine-grained tag from the tagger, more specific than the class; may mark tense, number etc. tag=PASS finds passives. In layers without tags (spaCy, Stanza), tag= also looks at the class (UPOS/XPOS). tag=A|B finds A or B.
glossary.token: Token: each word or punctuation mark isolated by the tokeniser.
glossary.upos: Universal POS: 17 word classes shared across languages (NOUN, VERB, ADJ...), from the Universal Dependencies project.
glossary.xpos: Language/treebank-specific POS (Penn Treebank for English); more detailed than UPOS.
glossary.z_score: z-score: how many standard deviations a value is above (+) or below (−) the mean. Here, the pattern's rate in your text relative to the reference texts.

writing.title: Writing
writing.subtitle: Compare your own text with a reference corpus. The result is descriptive: it shows what stands out from the corpus pattern — not proof about a population.
writing.formats: Accepts txt, md, docx and odt. For pdf, install the pypdf package.
writing.ref_none: No reference available — install a corpus or a list in Resources.
writing.need_text: Write or upload a text to compare.
writing.results: What stands out from the corpus pattern
writing.no_results: Nothing stood out with the current filters.
writing.limit_single: You compare ONE text with the corpus: a single unit, not a representative sample. Describe, don't generalise.
writing.limit_short: Short text: frequencies are unstable; read as a hint, not a firm result.
writing.limit_autocorr: Words within one text are not independent; so look at effect size (log ratio/%DIFF) together with the adjusted p.
writing.references: References: Dunning (1993); Kilgarriff (2001); Gabrielatos & Marchi (2012); Hardie (2014).
writing.about_sig: LL measures confidence that the difference is not chance; always with multiple-testing correction (FDR).
writing.about_mag: log ratio measures the size of the difference (the effect), not the confidence.
writing.about_disp: In how many reference texts the word appears: low = concentrated in few texts, may be an outlier.
writing.limit_sig: Significance (LL/adjusted p) tells confidence; magnitude (log ratio/%DIFF) tells size. Look at both.
writing.limit_disp: Low dispersion = the word appears in few reference texts; may be an isolated case, not a corpus pattern.
writing.warn.no_reference_docs: The reference has no dispersion info; cannot show in how many texts words appear.
writing.error.pdf_unavailable: To read PDF, install the pypdf package (pip install pypdf) or convert the file to txt.
writing.error.unsupported_format: Unsupported format: use txt, md, docx, odt or pdf.
writing.tab_words_hint: Which words stand out from the corpus pattern.
writing.tab_patterns_hint: Which part-of-speech patterns your text uses — richer than counting words.
writing.patterns_what: A construction is a pattern of classes, not a word: e.g. DET+ADJ+NOUN ("the new policy") or VERB+ADP ("depends on"). Comparing patterns shows how the text is built, even when the topic drives the vocabulary.
writing.about_z: How many standard deviations this pattern's rate in your text is above (positive) or below (negative) the mean of the reference texts. Descriptive.
writing.patterns_no_results: No pattern stood out with the current filters.
writing.warn.short_patterns: Short text ({words} words): the construction profile is indicative only.
writing.error.patterns_need_corpus: Constructions need a project corpus with a class layer (the .tsv list stores words, not patterns).
writing.error.patterns_tagger: This corpus was tagged with {tool}; for constructions, use a corpus tagged with spaCy.
writing.collocates_what: Collocates are the words that go together. Comparing what your text pairs with a word and what the reference usually pairs shows writing choices.
writing.collocates_hint: Click a word to see what goes with it.
writing.node_freq: {n}× in your text · {m}× in the reference
writing.lexis_what: Descriptive measures of vocabulary and sentence length. MTLD and Guiraud are less sensitive to text size than the type/token ratio (TTR).
writing.ddl_note: DDL tip: click “See in corpus” on a result and look at real concordances in the reference to draw your own conclusions.
writing.examples_hint: Click a result to see examples in the text and the corpus, with classes coloured.
writing.chart_hint: Positive: more in your text; negative: less. Distance from the reference pattern (z). Click an item to see examples.
writing.reference_not_corpus: Only examples from your text (the reference is not a project corpus).
